semanticOperations.before:
The in-widget settings panel supports location (name, latitude, longitude), calculation
method, Asr school, 12/24-hour, date format, and temperature units. A **location pin** beside
the location field shows the source — **red** = estimated from your IP (the default),
**glowing** = precise GPS (tap it to request browser permission), **grey** = manually set.
semanticOperations.after:
The in-widget settings panel supports location (name, latitude, longitude), calculation
method, Asr school, 12/24-hour, date format, and temperature units. A **location pin** beside
the location field identifies an estimated area, browser/saved browser position, or manually
selected site. Its title reports available accuracy in metres and original fix age; tap it
to request a browser position.

semanticOperations.before:
- **Precise location is optional and user-triggered.** The "Use precise location" button asks
  your browser's permission (`navigator.geolocation`) — it is **never** called automatically.
  In an iframe it usually requires `allow="geolocation"` on the `<iframe>` (the local-mode
  snippet from the builder includes it). If a host (e.g. TablissNG) strips that attribute or
  you deny permission, the widget falls back gracefully — coarse auto-detect and manual setup
  still work.
semanticOperations.after:
- **Browser location is optional and user-triggered.** The location pin requests one browser position after permission. Its reported accuracy may be known in metres or unknown; five decimal places do not measure accuracy. In an iframe, the local snippet includes `allow="geolocation"`, and the embedding parent's Permissions Policy and user grant also apply. Stripping delegation or restricting parent policy can block acquisition; coarse/manual setup remains available.
- **Acquisition and saving are separate.** A browser position retains its original acquisition time and reported accuracy; a saved browser position is a stored target and does not establish current presence. Saving settings does not renew a fix. Missing, malformed, nonpositive or future acquisition timestamps stay unknown; future timestamps have zero skew allowance against `Date.now()`. Portable URLs describe a configured destination and omit private acquisition history.

semanticOperations.before:
- **Saved settings stay local** to your browser/profile. If storage is blocked or partitioned
  (private browsing, strict third-party-iframe storage), saving is unavailable — the widget
  says so and your changes still apply **for the current session** (it never crashes).
semanticOperations.after: - **Storage outcome is measured.** Saved settings use this browser's storage. If writing is unavailable, changes still apply for the current session and Settings shows a retained warning. A partition can be writable and retain settings within that partition. Saving and persistence depend on the host's actual storage permissions and lifetime; blocked writes cause the session-only warning.

semanticOperations.before:
- **TablissNG:** coarse auto-detect works inside the iframe if your network/ad-blocker allows
  the request; precise location works only if TablissNG preserves `allow="geolocation"`;
  saved settings persist only if it doesn't partition iframe storage. All three degrade
  gracefully when not available.
semanticOperations.after: - **TablissNG conditions.** Coarse acquisition depends on permitted provider access; browser position depends on preserved delegation, parent policy and user grant; saving depends on writable host storage and its lifetime. These conditions are not a claim that a particular TablissNG version or partition policy has been qualified.

semanticOperations.before:
- **`WidgetConfig`**: `{v, lat, lon, tz, label, method, school, time, datefmt, units, lp, seed, source, savedAt}`,
  `source ∈ {hash, localStorage, coarse-ip, browser-geolocation, manual, fallback}`. Persisted under
  `salah_widget:config:v1` (separate from the prayer/weather caches; every access wrapped in try/catch).
semanticOperations.after:
- **`WidgetConfig`**: `{v, lat, lon, tz, label, method, school, time, datefmt, units, appearance, lp, seed, source, origin, savedAt, locationEvidence}`.
  `source ∈ {hash, localStorage, coarse-ip, browser-geolocation, place, manual, fallback}`; `origin`, when present,
  preserves the acquisition origin independently of the storage marker. Persisted under `salah_widget:config:v1`
  (separate from prayer/weather caches; every access wrapped in try/catch).
- **Location evidence:** `{intent, source, accuracyM, acquiredAt, provider, area, bounds}`.
  `intent ∈ {fixed-site, device-position, coarse-area, unknown}` and evidence
  `source ∈ {hash, manual, place, browser-geolocation, coarse-ip, legacy, unknown}`. Coordinates select the
  target; this record does not certify the viewer's current presence. Browser `accuracyM` is finite numeric
  metres ≥ 0 or `null` (a reported 0 stays 0); decimal places do not establish accuracy. `acquiredAt` is a finite
  numeric epoch > 0 and ≤ actual `Date.now()`, or `null`. The future-timestamp skew allowance is zero;
  missing/nonpositive/future/malformed time stays unknown, never an age-0 clamp. `provider`/`area` retain
  available text bounded to 80/240 characters. `bounds` is `{south,north,west,east}` with finite ordered
  latitudes in [-90,90] and longitudes in [-180,180], or `null`; no radius is invented.
- **Fix and persistence lifecycle:** `savedAt` is successful settings-write time, separate from `acquiredAt`.
  Saving label/units/method cannot renew a fix. Label/reverse naming retains compatible evidence; coordinate
  edits choose a manual fixed site and clear incompatible acquisition claims. Legacy records retain usable
  coordinates/preferences without substituting `savedAt`; reads do not destructively rewrite them. Saving
  browser-derived targets retains private evidence but downgrades the top-level source for old readers to a
  configured site. Portable hashes describe a fixed configured destination and omit private acquisition history.
  Denied persistence preserves useful in-memory metadata and prior saved bytes with the session-only warning;
  a writable partition may persist within its own permissions and lifetime. No new freshness/radius threshold
  or continuous location tracking follows from this schema.

preservedDeliveredR0010Preferences.text: A generic `#local=1` embed chooses method and units automatically after area detection. A local embed exported by the builder includes the selected method and temperature units as defaults for a viewer with no saved configuration, for example `#local=1&method=2&units=f`. An existing saved configuration in that viewer’s browser takes priority over those defaults. The generic preset remains `#local=1`.
